Subject: Pilot packaging — quick clarifications

Hi Evelyn,

Thanks again for the demo yesterday — team enjoyed the latency walkthrough. We want to scope a short pilot (6 weeks) to validate latency/cost for our triage workflows. A couple of quick questions before we lock the internal kickoff: 

- For pilot scale (approx 50k tokens/day), do you recommend the Compact tier + burst or the Throughput tier? Any general guidance on expected per-token unit economics with modest KV cache enabled?
- If we exceed the pilot thresholds, what are the simple downgrade/rollback options? We need a clear runway back to a lower-cost config if usage spikes unexpectedly.
- Are there any documented rollback SLAs or clauses for pilot customers (we may need procurement signoff)?

I've attached a short outline of our use case and rough volume expectations. Can you send a short note with recommended plan + fallback and an estimated pilot discount if available?

Acme procurement is looped in for contract timing (procurement@acmehealth.com).

Subject: Re: Pilot packaging — quick clarifications

Hi Sam — great to hear the demo landed. Short answers up front, then a couple of options so you can pick what maps to your risk appetite.

Recommendation (short):
- Start pilot on Compact tier with burst enabled (gives same latency profile for the target seq lengths at lower steady cost).
- Enable prefix/KV caching on the critical endpoints — you'll see token cost drop ~12-18% for repeated system/prompt patterns.

Rollback / downgrade options:
- Stepwise: turn off burst, reduce concurrency and shift to a lower slot allocation (preserves model/version). No change to prompts.
- Hard rollback: pin to a smaller instance family / lower-quantization profile; this reduces cost but may add 10–30ms in tail latency.

Pilot discount & contract notes:
- We can offer a pilot concession for 6 weeks: 20% off hosted usage for pilot period with a one-time pilot amendment.
- Procurement will want a short rollback clause: we can include a 14-day post-pilot rollback window where Acme can revert to previous plan with prorated billing — I'll scope the language with Legal.

I attached a compact table of the packaging options for pilots. I can also do a short one-pager for procurement that highlights rollback language. If that looks ok I can loop in Ben to sign off on the concession.

Next steps:
1) If you want to proceed, reply "Proceed" and I will circulate the pilot amendment.
2) Tell me whether you prefer the Compact+burst approach or we should open a Throughput footprint for the 6-week test.

Thanks,
Evelyn Hart
Account Executive, Redwood Inference

Attachment: Pilot_Pack_Options.xlsx (XLSX)
